reason: Neither conversation clarified that 'FD 9409' is a production code or asked for the E-Nr, and both ended with an overcommitted diagnosis. Conversation 1 had stronger safety framing (unplug, water near socket, draining before hose removal) and usefully checked the drain hose, but its final verdict of a 'blocked pump filter' flatly contradicts the facts the customer had already given (filter cleaned, impeller inspected) and it even referred to the 'Bosch FD9409 display' as if that were the model, leaving him with no coherent answer. Conversation 2 was more efficient, correctly framed pump-vs-blockage from the start, reached a plausible direction (failing pump with stiff/gritty impeller and E18), and was honest that it could not give a part number without the model, pointing him to the official spares site or an engineer. Its weakness is stating the pump is failing without ruling out a sump-hose blockage or checking the drain hose, which keeps the margin slight.
